Apple
秋季新品發表會
2026.09

### Page 2

iPhone 18 Pro與iPhone 18 Pro Max推出
• 蘋果新一代高階旗艦智慧型手機 ，在智慧功能、處理效能、電池續航與攝影系統四方面迎來
重大突破。外觀及材質採用同色調配色的鋁金屬邊框結合一體成型背面玻璃 ，提供4種配色，
包括太空黑、銀色、冰川藍以及勃根地紅。
• 螢幕互動介面：動態島縮小，支援同時顯示多達 3 個即時動態。
• Siri AI整合：由最新的Apple Foundation Models與端側模型驅動，具備擬真人聲、自訂語
速抑揚頓挫、螢幕感知、跨App執行指令與全系統精確聽寫。
• iPhone接力通話：允許兩部 iPhone共享同一個電話號碼 ，拿起任一部手機即能無縫通話
（首波與T-Mobile、德國電信合作，後續納入Verizon與EE）。
• AirDrop速度提升達 80%，行動網路與 Wi-Fi 自動無縫切換。
1
AAPL
資料來源： AAPL、中信投顧整理

### Page 3

18 pro系列核心處理器升級：A20 Pro 晶片
• 先進製程：採用最新2nm製程技術打造，具備更高的電晶體密度。
• 6核心CPU：配置2顆桌面級全新超級核心，效能提升達20%，為智慧型手機中最快核心；搭配4顆
高能效核心，並全數整合神經加速器以驅動低延遲裝置端AI。
• 7核心GPU：圖形運算效能較前代大幅躍升 40%，微架構針對3A級手遊優化；配備全新神經加速
器，其8位元浮點運算吞吐量提升達2倍，可於本機直接運行第三方大型語言模型。
• 雙神經網路引擎：額外配置第二組神經網路引擎，核心總數達32核心，本機AI運算能力倍增。
• 記憶體介面：記憶體頻寬大幅提升50%，為 iPhone 歷來最寬的記憶體匯流排介面。
• WMCM封裝：借鑒Apple M系列晶片架構，採用全新特製封裝，將晶圓裸晶與記憶體並排佈局，
移出SoC主要熱路徑，使晶粒直接與均熱板貼合，提升散熱效能。
2
AAPL
資料來源： AAPL、中信投顧整理

### Page 4

散熱系統與續航快充
• 新一代散熱Vapor Chamber：表面積為iPhone 17 Pro的3倍，內部去離子水持續循環導熱；
均熱板採用80%回收不銹鋼製成，並搭配高導熱石墨片。
• 奈米雙晶銅材料：業界首創散熱材料 ，能增強機身結構剛性，並快速將熱量自顯示螢幕引導
排除。
• 持續效能釋放：高負載下持續效能較iPhone 17 Pro提升 40%，為iPhone 16 Pro及更早機
型的2倍。
• 電池續航力：(1)iPhone 18 Pro：機身小巧，但擁有與iPhone 17 Pro Max相同的全天候續
航；純 eSIM 機型之影片播放時間達 36 小時；真實綜合日常使用模型下可達 24小時。(2)
iPhone 18 Pro Max純eSIM機型影片播放時間高達 45 小時；綜合使用模型下每次充電可達
30 小時。有線快速充電：充電約 15 分鐘可充至 50% 電量；充電 5 分鐘可提供約 6 小時影
片播放時間。
3
AAPL
資料來源： AAPL、中信投顧整理

### Page 5

專業相機系統
• 4,800萬像素Fusion主相機：搭載可變光圈 ，採用6片雷射切割葉片 ，葉片厚度薄於人類頭髮 ，由特製聚
合物複合材料製成；搭配微型轉子機構與客製光學鏡片組。
• 可調節光圈：暗光環境自動切換至 F1.8 大光圈，進光量增加約 50%，提升夜間人像與星空攝影品質；光
線充足時縮小光圈以加深景深，確保群體合照邊角與前後背景清晰。
• Pro Controls：提供相機手動操作介面，支援手動微調4檔光圈、白平衡、直方圖曝光監控、手動快門速
度調整。
• 錄影與對焦升級：支援拍攝後添加電影級景深且開放60 FPS半速慢動作；支援4K Dolby Vision HDR縮時
攝影；Audio Mix升級聲音與音樂演算法；智慧對焦追蹤利用AI本機模型牢牢鎖定進出畫面的動態主體。
• 攝影風格升級：新增照片紋理與膠卷顆粒感調節，可即時調整膚質質感並支援無損復原。
• 影像真實性：除相容SynthID標記AI生成圖外，推出Apple Reference Image憑證機制。感光元件在拍攝

瞬間即在像素層級對照片進行安全密碼學簽署 ，私有雲端運算會沖印成一份不可修改的數位負片 ，與一
般可編輯相片共同儲存於照片App中，以證明照片原始未經變造。

AAPL

### Page 6

蘋果首款摺疊旗艦：iPhone Duo
• 蘋果推出首款旗艦摺疊機iPhone Duo，將iPad級別的大螢幕整合至小巧機身中，採書本式對折，非對稱
式對角圓角線條，展開時為iPhone歷來最薄機身，核心組件高度整合在相機凸起處內部 ，留出內部空間
配置雙電池模組。螢幕正面為Ceramic Shield 2、背面為Ceramic Shield，並具備完整IP68等級防塵防水。
• 機身：邊框由5級鈦金屬精工切削並呈現拋光鏡面質感；天線斷點處導入 陶瓷纖維增強嵌件強度為5級鈦
金屬的3倍。
• 內外螢幕：展開為7.6 吋Super Retina XDR螢幕，具窄邊框與一致的長寬比，外螢幕：5.4 吋顯示螢幕，
具備相當於iPhone 18 Pro 90%的可用顯示面積。內螢幕影片可播放31小時，外螢幕播放達44小時，雙
螢幕平均綜合使用續航達24小時。
• 後置鏡頭：4,800萬像素 Fusion 主鏡頭(支援2x光學品質望遠、4K 120 FPS慢動作錄影與4K杜比視界縮
時)+4,800 萬像素 Fusion超廣角鏡頭。

• Apple Pencil支援：雙螢幕皆支援Apple Pencil(USB-C)，為iPhone首度支援Apple Pencil手寫與繪圖。
• 側邊Touch ID：於側邊電源鍵整合TouchID指紋辨識(可註冊多組指紋)，亦支援Apple Watch自動解鎖。

### Page 7

iPhone Duo雙晶片架構，A20 Pro及自研C2晶片
6
AAPL
資料來源： AAPL、中信投顧整理
• A20 Pro晶片：採用2奈米與裸晶直貼散熱封裝 ，配合大型均熱板，持續效能較 iPhone 17
Pro提升35%；內建全新顯示引擎 ，可同時驅動雙螢幕並消除螢幕下鏡頭邊緣像素過渡走樣 。
• Apple C2晶片：深度整合基頻、RF收發器、PMIC與通訊韌體，上傳速率較上一代C1X提升
達50%，功耗降低15%。在美國市場正式加入5G mmWave頻段支援。
• 全eSIM架構與雙電池：全球市場全面採純 eSIM配置；機身兩側各配置一組高能量密度電池 ，
由客製晶片與演算法自動調配充放平衡。

### Page 8

iPhone Duo無摺痕螢幕技術
• 鉸鏈：由超過100枚精密微型零組件與碳纖維承載支撐板組成 ，可變扭力曲線讓開闔阻尼手
感順暢，並整合磁鐵陣列牢固吸合。
• 螢幕防護多層貼合結構：表面採用奈米紋理抗眩光表面 ，利用無光罩雷射微影技術逐像素雕
刻微透鏡，呈現視覺平整霧面感，使中央摺痕在視覺上近乎隱形 。表層覆蓋高抗刮客製聚合
物，剛性提升40%。OLED面板上下皆夾有高強度超薄玻璃 ，並灌注黏彈性膠材 ，摺疊時各
層能如書頁滑移，避免反覆摺疊疲勞形變；底層襯有鈦金屬板強化支撐。
• 雷射製造公差控制：組裝以AI演算法將鉸鏈與外殼進行公差吻合配對；出廠前以共軛焦雷射
逐台掃描表面拓撲，並3D列印沉積多達25層光固化聚合物微層，消除微波紋。

AAPL

### Page 10

新一代無線藍芽耳機AirPods 5
• 全新第5代半開放式真無線耳機，正式在全線AirPods系列中全面普及主動式降噪，降噪效能
比前代提升 50%。延續半開放式配戴設計，重新設計內部構造，貼合各類耳形幾何結構。
• 多孔聲學架構：全新多孔內部聲學管道 ，搭配新一代適應性等化功能 ，大幅提升低頻飽滿度
與高頻細節。
• 個人化空間音訊：提供包圍感更強的動態頭部追蹤空間音訊體驗。
• 通透模式與適應性音訊通透模式更加自然；適應性音訊能根據周圍環境噪音強度 ，在主動降
噪與通透模式之間即時自動混合調配。
• Apple Intelligence與Siri AI整合：可免持利用語音調用Siri AI，結合個人脈絡資料解答疑問；
支援即時翻譯功能。

AAPL

### Page 11

Apple Watch Series 12/Apple Watch Ultra 4
• Apple Watch Series 12搭載新一代 S11 晶片，首度採二代Ceramic Shield 2，螢幕耐刮耐摔強度比前代
Ion-X玻璃高 60%。
• 電極接觸面積擴增：在相同錶背面積下增加電極表面積，提升ECG心電圖偵測的皮膚導電與接觸精準度。
• 環狀光電二極體陣列：重新設計的光電二極體以環狀結構排列，大幅提升對反射光線的捕捉效率。
• 全新健康App功能：(1)由 Apple Intelligence 自動生成個人生理趨勢摘要(如睡眠走勢或 VO2 Max 峰值)，
並動態給出間歇跑等運動調整建議 。(2)將體能指標與血檢生物標記對比實際年齡 ，分析日常習慣之健康
影響。(3)全方位量化睡眠、活動與心臟表現，支援手動同步病歷，或以 119 美元向Quest訂購50項生物
標記的血檢套裝，並在本機結合專家影片給出醫學解讀。(4)搭配iPhone相機與Apple Watch感測器，即

時語音校正關節動作，輔助 VO2 Max 測試或運動傷害復健進度追蹤。
• Apple Watch Ultra 4：為極限運動、專業冒險家與耐力賽事選手設計之頂級智慧手錶，日常一般使用續
航時間達2天以上。全功能開啟狀態(完整心率追蹤+全頻雙頻GPS)下，體能訓練時間達18小時。

### Page 12

相關台股供應鏈
• 全新(2455)、穩懋(3105)：因Wi-Fi 7相較於Wi-Fi 6在手機中新增6GHz的頻段，同時由於對PA性能要求，
將轉向使用GaAs作為材料。我們認為相關供應鏈如全新(2455)、穩懋(3105)，將受惠於手機廠導入Wi-Fi 7
，下半年PA相關台股供應鏈營運展望正向，若後續iPhone新機銷售表現佳，有望進一步對獲利有所挹注。
• 大立光(3008)：大立光受惠iPhone 18新機拉貨動能，且今年新旗艦機首度搭載可變光圈鏡頭，並且為主要
供應商，為2H26營運增加動能。大立光切入CPO應用，有利於推升評價，雖短期營收能見度有限，但預估
將於2028年實現量產並貢獻營收，有望成為自手機鏡頭外公司第二成長動能。過往大立光在手機鏡頭本業
的營運上升週期下 ，預估本益比約交易在 15至18倍左右，而公司成功切入CPO元件市場，市場現給予25-
30倍以上本益比左右。
• 奇鋐(3017)：過去iPhone 17 Pro 首度導入超薄 VC，隨AI 負載提升，我們預期 VC 將逐步成為蘋果高階手

機、平板及折疊旗艦標配。折疊機預計採用雙片式超薄VC，帶動單機用量與ASP倍增；我們預期奇鋐可取
得約50%市占率，有望明顯受惠於蘋果高階手持裝置散熱需求成長。
• 新日興(3376)：在折疊機軸承(Hinge)方面，Apple為實現極致的無感摺痕與耐用度 ，軸承內部結構更為複
雜，零件數及加工精度均較現有非蘋產品大幅提升，帶動單機軸承模組 ASP 接近倍增。台系供應鏈中，我
們認為新日興(3376)受惠程度最高。新日興與主要組裝代工廠鴻海(2317) 透過合資關係合作，有助於整合
機構件製造與組裝，並提升初期量產良率；我們預期其有望取得 Apple 首款折疊機的高階軸承訂單，成為
新日興中長期獲利的重要成長動能。
• 鴻海(2317): 鴻海負責蘋果首款摺疊機的整機組裝與最終調整，並與軸承廠新日興深化合作，共同搶攻高精
密轉軸商機。高毛利的新機效應將顯著拉抬整體產品組合與獲利表現。結合 AI 伺服器業務的持續高成長，
未來營運展望樂觀。

前次投資建議：2026.08.10 
「買進」 ，目標價: $252

報告日期：2026.09.10 研 究 員：邱岳霖

摘 要 及 調 整 原 因 
➢ AI 導線架動能強勁，車市需求回溫，均熱片新案發酵，2026 年將重返榮耀，EPS 7.4元 
➢ AI 產品全面放量，均熱片進度優於預期，車用穩健成長，2027 年獲利倍增，上修 EPS 至
15.2 元，考量到今年獲利上修且未來長期營運動能強勁，維持「買進」投資評等，目標價調
升至 410 元(27X 27(F)PER)，潛在上漲空間 72.6%。

基本資料 結論與建議 
2026/9/9 收盤價： 237.50 ➢ 展望 2026 年，順德最大成長動能來自  AI 產品線，
目前逾 60 支新產品開案，在擴產效益帶動下，預期今
年 AI 相關營收倍數增長；均熱片近期已通過 4 間大
客戶認證，新增 4 台高噸位沖床與 15 台 CNC，並
年底達 100 萬片月產能、明年中達 2,000 萬片目標，
惟現階段量小、今年挹注不大。毛利率受惠  26H1 漲
價、稼動率高檔與產品組合轉佳，加上下半年客戶加價
搶產能，上修預估。綜上，兆豐投顧上修 2026年稅後
淨利 14.4 億元，YoY +374.4%，EPS 7.4 元。 
➢ 展望 2027 年，隨單機櫃功耗自數十 kW 往 100 kW 
以上，產業加速朝 HVDC 架構演進，順德憑藉與歐美
大廠合作開發的高功率、高散熱、高可靠度導線架成為
主要受惠者 ， AI 導線架營收可望隨  ± 400V/800V 
HVDC 滲透率提升而續強；均熱片進度優於研究部預
期，2,000 萬片有機會於 27 年中到位，隨 NPI 專案
逐步落地，27H2 動能將顯著增長，並隨 CPU/GPU 大
尺寸擴張成為新一輪成長主軸。在組合優化與稼動率維
持高檔下，毛利率可望續揚，兆豐投顧上修順德 2027 
年營收 206.4 億元(原估 155 億元)，YoY +45.7%，
毛利率 24.1%(原估 21.3%)，年增 2.8ppt，稅後淨利 
29.4 億元，YoY +104.5%，EPS 15.2 元(原估 8.4

個股報告 
資料來源：CMoney；兆豐投顧預估

營 運 分 析

順德 2025年跨入 AI server領域，2026年散熱領域正式發酵 
順德(2351)成立於 1967 年，以辦公文具起家，1983 年跨入半導體導線架，
並於 2010 年與日本三菱伸銅(mitsubishi-shindoh)技術合作，取得導線架原
料銅合金製程設備及技術授權，目前產品涵蓋 IC 導線架、功率/分離式元件
導線架、LED 導線架、音圈馬達彈片，終端應用遍及車用、工業與消費性電
子。順德目前在全球導線架市佔排名前五，而在 Power IC 導線架則排名第
一。順德過往多以車用產品為主，不過隨著資料中心電源架構的改變，順德
與英飛凌將 800V 車用電源管理經驗移轉至資料中心，順德成為全台唯一 AI 
server 導線架主力供應商，並於 2025 年開始量產高功率導線架與穩壓器。
而順德自 2024 年布局均熱片跨足散熱領域，並於 2026 年開始生產 CPO 
Switch產品，而多家 CSP 之 CPU與 GPU 也有望於本年度驗證後開始出貨，
預期均熱片月產能從 26年底 100萬片大幅拉升至 27年 2,000萬片(不含 NPI
產品需求規劃)，反映 AI導線架與均熱片需求大幅增長，順德於中國江蘇廠、
台灣彰化廠與南投廠同步擴產，並新購大噸位沖床，同時也在台灣與馬來西
亞找地新建廠房以因應未來幾年高壓電源與均熱片之高速成長期。

- 3 - 
個股報告 
AI 導線架供不應求，輔以銅價上漲與客戶加價搶購，上修 26Q3 EPS至 2.3 
元 
順德(2351)公告 8月營收：營收 13.3 億元，MoM -0.1%/YoY +61.2%，為單
月次高，Q3達成率 69%，遠優研究部預期，未能再創高係因消費性包括 VCM
與文具類產品較上月有所衰退，不過預期在車用需求全面復甦與 AI 導線架
供不應求，Q3營收可望再創高至 36.5 億元，QoQ +3%/YoY +43.6%，車
用方面：除歐美車廠需求延續外，陸系新品也將推出，預期車用成長動能將
延續，此外 AI導線架於 Q2有近 30%季增長，預期在新產能開出下，營收將
逐月創高，而在產品組合優化與稼動率提升下，同時 AI 導線架供不應求使客
戶加價搶產能，故上修毛利率至 22%(原估 20%)，季增1.3ppt，年增9.6ppt，
同步上修稅後淨利 4.4 億元，QoQ +45.6%/YoY +405.2%，EPS 2.3 元 (原
估 1.8元)。

AI 導線架動能強勁，車市需求明顯回溫，均熱片新案持續發酵，2026 年將
重返榮耀，EPS 7.4元 
展望 2026 年，順德最大成長動能來自 AI 產品線，隨著伺服器電源架構改
變，PSU 瓦數持續提升，高功率導線架需求將被徹底激發，從高壓電網、
SST(固態變壓器)、Power Stage、48V bus converter、800V HVDC 與 BBU 
皆須用到高功率導線架，而順德自 2024 年攜手英飛凌將 800V 車用電源管
理經驗移轉至資料中心 ，使順德成為全球  AI server 導線架主力供應商之
一，目前有超過 60 支新產品開案，同時在擴產效益帶動下，預期 2026 年
AI 相關營收將倍數增長；在車用方面，受惠庫存調整結束，同時電動車需求
激增與新車款推出，預期全年呈雙位數增長；在均熱片方面，公司耕耘近兩
年，近期已通過 4 間大客戶認證，除新增 4 台高噸位沖床外也同步增加 15
台 CNC 設備，同時也於近期租賃新廠房以滿足年底 100 萬片月產能需求，
並於明年中達成 2,000 萬片產能目標，公司放眼價值更高 NPI，研究部認為
產業最具指標之共平面度，順德已能做至 30μm 以下，名列產業前茅，預期
將受客戶大幅青睞，更大尺寸產品用於 ASIC/CPU/GPU 均熱片有望陸續驗
證出貨，惟現階段出貨量較小且產能有限，預期今年對營運挹注不大。毛利
率方面：受惠 26H1 漲價帶動，稼動率維持高檔，同時產品組合轉佳下，且
下半年客戶加價搶產能 ，上修毛利率預估。綜上所述，兆豐投顧上修順德  
2026 年營收 142 億元，YoY +3 8.3%，毛利率 21.3%，年增 8ppt，稅後
淨利 14.4 億元，YoY +374.4%，EPS 7.4元。

AI 產品全面放量，均熱片進度優於預期，車用穩健成長，2027 年獲利倍增，
EPS 15.2 元 
展望 2027 年，隨著單機櫃功耗自數十 kW 往 100 kW 以上，過往 48V/54V 
供電架構已不敷使用，故產業正加速朝 HVDC(高壓直流)架構演進，順德憑
藉與歐美大廠合作開發的高功率、高散熱、高可靠度的導線架，將成為主要

壹、投 資 建 議

一、 2Q26 營收 、獲利創高， EPS 7.43 元 
廣達 2Q26 營收 1.04 兆， QoQ +28.1% ，YoY +105.6% ，受 惠於
伺 服 器、 筆電 第二季 均 呈 現雙 位 數 的成長 。 產 品 組 合 部 分 ， 伺 服
器 佔 整 體 營 收 8 成 ， 其 中 ，AI 伺 服 器 對 整 體 伺 服 器 營 收 貢 獻約
75%~80% ，筆電 則佔 整體營收的 低雙位數百分比。 筆電部分，
2Q26 筆 電 出 貨 量1,150 萬 台 ，QoQ + 15% ，YoY  -5%。2Q26 筆
電 出 貨 優 於預 期 ， 主 要 由 於客 戶 新 機 種 的 拉 貨 動 能 延 續 至 第 二
季， 以及 各 品 牌 客 戶預期 記 憶 體 價 格 持 續 上 漲而 提 前 拉 貨。 而獲
利 方 面，2Q26 營 業 毛 利520 .8 億，QoQ +34.6 %。YoY + 46.6 %，
毛 利 率 5.0%，QoQ +0.2ppts，YoY -2.0ppts，營 業 利 益342 .4 億，
QoQ +48.7 %，YoY +67.8 %，營 利 率 3.3 %，QoQ +0.45 ppts，YoY 
-0.75 ppts 。公 司 表 示，高階 AI 機櫃對 公司 毛 利 的 稀 釋，隨著 產品
組合優化 影響 逐步 降 低 ， 以 及 2Q26 費 用 率 降 至 歷 史 新 低 的
1.72% ， 帶 動 營 利 率 獲 得 改 善 。2Q26 業 外 淨 利 23.2 億 ， 稅 後 淨
利 286.5 億， QoQ +35.2 %，YoY + 69.9 %， 單 季 稅 後EPS 7.43
元。

二、 3Q26  AI 伺服器動能延續，筆電面臨 逆風  
公司 公告 7 月 營 收 3399 億， MoM -6.3% ，YoY +120.7% ，今年
累 計 營 收2.21 兆， YoY +79.6% 。展望 3Q26 ， 公司 預期 AI 伺服
器 營 收 持 續 強 勁 增 長 ， 但 因 第 二 季 基 期 已 拉 高 ， 季 增 幅 度 會 低 於
第 二 季 。此 外 ， 公 司 表 示 ，第 三 季 起部 分 客 戶 專 案將由 Buy and Sell 
模 式 轉 為Consignment 模式，將 有 助 於 大 幅 減 輕 營 運 資 金 壓 力 並
舒 緩 毛 利 率 稀 釋影響 。 筆 電 部 分 ， 由 於 主 要客 戶 已 於 上 半 年 提 前
拉 貨，再加上 記 憶 體 與CPU 成 本 大 漲，壓 抑 終 端 採 購 意 願，預計
第 三 季 出 貨 量 將 季 減 逾20% 。 預估 3Q26 營收 1.05 兆 ，QoQ 
+1.5 %，YoY + 112.5 %， 毛 利 率 5.1%， 營 利 率 3.3%， 稅 後 淨 利
288 億 元 ， 單 季 稅 後EPS 7.46 元。

三、預估 2026/2027 年 EPS 27.50 /31.63 元 
展望 2026 年 ， 公 司 表 示 ，AI 伺 服 器 訂 單 能 見 度 已到 2028 年，
維持 今年 全年 AI 伺 服 器營 收 倍 增預期 不 變，而 通 用 伺 服 器亦 維持
全 年 營 收 雙 位 數 年 增 目 標 。筆 電 部 分 ，儘 管 上 半 年 連 續 兩 季 出 貨
表 現 優 於 預 期 ，但 由 於客 戶 提 前 備 貨且 缺 料 情 況在 下 半 年 未 見 明
顯改善 ，公司 預 估 下 半 年 出 貨 將 低 於 上 半 年 ，全 年 筆 電 出 貨 量 預

在 生 成 式AI 商 機 快 速 擴 張 帶 動 下，全 球 雲 端 基 礎 設 施 投 資 進 入 新
一 輪 高 峰 。 亞 馬 遜 、Alphabet 和 微 軟 認 為 其 在 先 前 的 鉅 額 投 資 已
帶 動 營 收 明 顯 成 長 ， 同 時 預 估 未 來AI 潛 在 商 機 仍 持 續 擴 大 。 其 中，
亞 馬 遜、Alphabet 和 Meta 已 陸 續 上 調2026 全 年 投 資 金 額，且 四
大雲端服務供應商 (CSP )總資本支出將上升至 7,450 億美元新高
規模 。 亞 馬 遜 、 微 軟 、Alphabet 與 Meta 2026 年第 1、2 季分別
為 1,306 億、1,701 億 美 元，同 時 亞 馬 遜、Alphabet 和 Meta 再上
修 2026 全 年 資 本 支 出 金 額，2026 年 資 本 支 出預 估 將達 7,450 億
美元 。而 根據 TrendForce 最 新 產 業 研 究，全 球 主 要 雲 端 服 務 供 應
商(CSP) 為 加 速 建 置AI 基 礎 設 施 ， 資 本 支 出 預 估 於2026 年 將 年
增 98%，2027 年 再 成 長50% 至 1.3 兆 美 元 左 右，年 增 率 收 斂的 主
要 原因， 除了 反 映 高 基 期 因 素之外 ， 部 分 可 歸 咎 為鉅 額 資 本 支 出
對 四 大 CSP 財 務 衝 擊 日 益 擴 大。然 而， 在 AI Inference 、Agentic 
AI 、 自 研 ASIC 和 新 一 代AI 模 型 持 續 推 升 算 力 需 求 的 情 況 下 ， 預
期 整 體 CSP 投 資 金 額 將 續 創 新 高 紀 錄 ， 產 業 成 長 有 望 從 原 先 以
GPU 擴 張 為 主，轉 為 包 含AI server 、液 冷 散 熱、先 進 封 裝、高 速
互 聯 、 電 源 和 記 憶 體 等 基 礎 設 施 全 面 升 級 的 態 勢 。

2. 2026 年全球 AI 伺服器出貨量預計年增 31%  
根據 TrendForce 最新 AI server 產 業 研 究 ， 近 期 超 大 型CSP 、
Tier -2 資 料 中 心 業 者 對NVIDIA GB/VR 等 整 櫃 式AI server 方 案 的
採 購 意 願 明 顯 提 高 ， 且Google 、AWS 新 一 代 ASIC 平 台 於 2026
下 半 年 陸 續 放 量，加 上 中 系 業 者 擴 大 採 用 本 地AI 方 案 以 滿 足 雲 端
大 型 語 言 模 型(LLM ) AI 需 求 ， 促 使TrendForce 上調 2026 年 AI 
server 出 貨 年 成 長 幅 度，從 原 先 的28% 更 新 為 近31% 。北 美 五 大
業者 2026 年 的 資 本 支 出 多 翻 倍 提 升 ， 反 映 出 大 型CSP 廠 持 續 擴
建 AI 資 料 中 心、GPU 叢 集、液 冷 散 熱 等 新 一 代 基 礎 設 施，以 應 對
生成式 AI 及 大 型 模 型 快 速 成 長 帶 來 的 算 力 需 求 。其中， Google 
2026 至 2027 年 都 將 側 重 自 家TPU 晶 片 發 展 ，2027 年 出 貨 量 有
望 繼 續 高 速 成 長 。AWS 2026 年以 NVIDIA GB300 作為 GPU AI 
server 主 力，自 研 ASIC 也 穩 定 出 貨，預 期 至2027 年 量 能 將 再 擴
大。 Meta 2026 年 主 要 採 用NVIDIA GB/VR 、AMD Helios 整櫃式
方 案，自 研 ASIC 布 局 預 計 至2027 年 將 明 顯 加 速，為 該 公 司 長 期
降低 AI 基 礎 設 施 成 本 、 提 升 推 論 效 率 的 重 要 策 略 。

3. 2Q26 PC 出貨量 年減 4.9% ，蘋果 市佔率逆勢擴張  
根據 國 際 數 據 資 訊(IDC )報 告 ，2026 年 第 二 季 全 球PC 出 貨 總 量 達
6,820 萬 台、年 減 4.9% ，主 要 由 於 記 憶 體 短 缺 持 續 推 升 零 組 件 成
本 ， 再 加 上 總 體 經 濟 環 境 不 佳 ， 導 致 終 端 需 求 與 換 機 意 願 大 幅 放
緩，整 體 拉 貨 動 能 無 力 延 續。其 中，Apple 2Q26 PC 出 貨 量 為670
萬 台 ，YoY +10.1% ， 主 要 受 惠 於MacBook Neo 帶 動 。 此 外 ， 面
對 零 組 件 短 缺 與 成 本 攀 升 逆 風 ， 蘋 果 憑 藉 龐 大 採 購 規 模 與 供 應 鏈
優 勢 穩 固 供 貨 ， 使 其 市 佔 率 逆 勢 擴 張 。

Advantech  | Asia Pacific
August Sales -8% MoM/+88%
YoY
In this report, we focus on Advantech's monthly sales, which we
believe could be a catalyst for its share price.
Details:
• August sales were NT$10,419mn (-8% MoM/+88% YoY),
• QTD revenue reached 77% of MSe, at NT$28,185mn (+8% QoQ/+59% YoY),
and 76% of consensus, at NT$28,371mn (+9% QoQ/+60% YoY).
• By region, N.A (+106%) outperformed, while other markets, including Europe
(+52%), China (+67%), Taiwan (+96%), Japan (+73%), Korea (+79%)  and

emerging markets (+75%),  also performed strongly.
• By segment, Intelligent Systems was +93% YoY,   IoT Automation was +36%
YoY, while  Intelligent Service grew single-digit% YoY. The Embedded Sector
grew 61% YoY, of which Embedded IoT grew 83% YoY, while Applied
Computing grew 37% YoY.
Our view:
• We think its 3Q26 revenue is tracking ahead of market expectations and
more likely to approach 20-25% QoQ growth.
• Management attributed the strength in August to demand from sectors

including semi, AI datacenter, energy infrastructure, and factory automation.
• B/B ratio in August was stronger than that in July, continuing to point to a
strong revenue outlook in the coming quarters.
• We remain constructive on Advantech, as it is well positioned to benefit
from accelerating IoT market growth amid edge AI proliferation.

Valuation Methodology and Risks
Advantech (2395.TW)
Base case, 30x 2027e P/E. We view our target multiple as justified by our 30% earnings CAGR
forecast for 2025-28. It implies a PEG of 1.0, vs. the stock's average one-year forward P/E of
25x in 2015-22 and the earnings CAGR of 8% during that period, with a PEG of 3.5.
Risks to Upside
n Stronger-than-expected macroeconomic conditions
n More top- and bottom-line growth from the platform and applications

Risks to Downside
n Weaker macro environment
n Slower progress in edge AI implementation

12-18 months.
Equal-weight (E). The stock's total return is expected to be in line with the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over

the next 12-18 months.
Not-Rated (NR). Currently the analyst does not have adequate conviction about the stock's total return relative to the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage
universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next 12-18 months.
Underweight (U). The stock's total return is expected to be below the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next

12-18 months.

Chenbro  | Asia Pacific
August Sales Flat MoM/+41%
Y oY
In this report, we focus on Chenbro's monthly sales, which we
believe could be a catalyst for its share price.
Details:
• August  sales were NT$2,457mn (flat MoM/+41% YoY).
• QTD sales reached 59% of our 3Q26 estimate at NT$8,368mn (+7% QoQ/
+48% YoY) and 56% of consensus at NT$8,763mn (+12% QoQ/+55% YoY).
Our view:
• We see its 3Q26 revenue tracking slightly behind our estimate.
• We think near-term sentiment should remain lackluster amid the temporary

hiccup resulting from supply chain management.
• Management remains optimistic on the 2H26 outlook. The demand from its
GPU/ASIC server clusters and general servers is strong, driving  orders for its
chassis and rack offerings.

Valuation Methodology and Risks
Chenbro (8210.TW)
Base case, derived from 27x 2027e P/E. We view our target multiple as justified by the 33%
earnings CAGR we see for 2025-28, which implies a PEG of 0.8. This is in line the average of
0.8 over 2014-24, when the stock was trading at an average P/E of 12x for a 15% earnings
CAGR.
Risks to Upside
n Stronger AI capex outlook
n Larger market share gains within existing customers

n Faster penetration into new customers
n Higher entry barrier among peers that leads to higher ASP/profitability
n Better macro outlook
Risks to Downside
n Softer AI capex
n Less share gains within existing customers
n Slower penetration into new customers
n Intensifying competition leading to lower ASP/profitability
n Continuous macro uncertainties

MPI Corporation  | Asia Pacific
3Q Revenue Looks Better than
Feared; OW
MPI reported August sales of NT$2,048mn, +13% M/M and +70% Y/Y, above our
NT$1,876mn estimate –  mainly supported by price hikes, TPU, and other AI ASICs.
Assuming flat September revenue M/M, 3Q revenue would rise 13% Q/Q, above our
+7% estimate and the Street at +10% Q/Q.
Stay OW: As previously indicated, we expect 3Q revenue to exceed guidance given
CPC/VPC price hikes. With very strong micro bump demand and more migration to

2nm, we believe MPI needs to expand MEMS probe card capacity to at least 8–10mn
pins per month in 2027, positioning it to meet strong AI ASIC and GPU demand.
PCB material shortages remain a risk; however, MPI is diversifying suppliers and
seeking substitutes.
For CPO,  Insertion 2 qualification continues, with insertion 3 shipments on track to
start in 4Q26.
Investors were slightly frustrated by the conservative guidance, but still view MPI as
best positioned to benefit from increased chip probing demand over the longer term

Valuation Methodology and Risks
                        MPI Corporation (6223.TWO)                    
We derive our price target from a residual income model, as we believe this can best capture 
the long-term value. We assume a 9.78% cost of equity (risk-free rate 2.0% and risk premium 
6.0%), a payout ratio of 67%, a medium-term growth rate of 16.0%, and a terminal growth rate 
of 4.0%. Our price target implies 50x/25x 2027e/2028e P/E. We believe its valuation will con-
tinue to climb along with growing earnings.

## Document 091: 260909_daiwa_ardentec-buy-initiation

Source PDF: all report pdf/260909_daiwa_ardentec-buy-initiation.pdf
Report source: line報告備份
Date: 2026-09-09

Extraction status: ok

### Page 1

Taiwan Information Technology

Investment case: We initiate coverage of Ardentec, a Taiwanese pure 
testing provider serving foundries, IDMs and fabless chipmakers, with a 
Buy (1) rating. We believe Ardentec is transitioning from an auto/industrial 
test vendor into an AI/HPC wafer-sort powerhouse, supported by a 35% 
revenue CAGR (2025-28E) and gross margin expansion to 45% by 2028E.

Longtan fab ramp with premium hourly rate. We expect the 7-story 
Longtan mega-fab, which is developing at one floor per quarter to deliver 
significant revenue contribution (c.TWD450m+/quarter per floor). We 
believe this underpins a structural upgrade in revenue, as advanced wafer 
sorting for application-specific integrated circuits (ASIC) commands an 
hourly billing rate nearly double that of legacy testing. Furthermore, we 
believe strategic collaborations with key Taiwan foundry leaders position 
Ardentec to capture expanding AI/HPC test allocations moving forward.

Gross margin increase driven by high utilisation rate. As its key peers 
prioritise merchant AI GPUs, displaced mobile/RF/networking orders are 
refilling Ardentec’s fully depreciated tester lines, lifting mature utilisation. 
Test-time inflation (2-3x on complex ASICs) anchors Longtan capacity at a 
90%+ utilisation rate. As fixed costs comprise 40-45% of COGS, this drives 
blended gross margin from 36% in 2025 to 45% in 2028E, with steady 
operating expense (9-10% of sales) flowing into operating profit.

Turnkey E/O testing for CPO and non-dilutive expansion. Leveraging 
synergies with Giga-Solution, Raytek (7873 TT; 25% stake), and strategic 
partner Fabrinet (FN US, NR), Ardentec builds a comprehensive electro-
optical test flow aligned with TSMC’s compact universal photonic engine 
(COUPE) platform. While co-packaged optics (CPO) testing accounts for 
<5% of near-term sales, it secures an early-mover moat in optical I/O.

Catalysts: 1) Completion of 7-floor capacity with premium rates and higher 
UTR; 2) peer spillover orders refilling fully depreciated capacity, expanding 
gross margin; 3) higher-than-expected ASIC and CPO contribution.

Valuation: Driven by a structural earnings inflection fuelled by Longtan fab 
expansion, expanding AI ASIC test pricing premiums, and high-margin peer 
spillover orders, we initiate Ardentec with a Buy (1) rating and 12-month TP 
of TWD340, based on a target PER of 25x applied to our 4-quarter-forward

Ardentec (3264 TT): 9 September 2026 
From Automotive to AI/HPC growth engines 
A premier pure play in wafer testing 
Founded in October 1999 and headquartered in Hukou, Hsinchu, Ardentec Corporation is 
a premier semiconductor testing pure play, ranking among the top three pure test service 
providers in Taiwan in terms of revenue. While semiconductor testing is inherently a 
capital- and technology-intensive arena dominated by foundry and integrated OSAT titans 
such as TSMC (2330 TT, TWD2,465, Buy [1]; covered by Daiwa analyst Rick Hsu) and 
ASE Group (3711 TT, TWD640, Outperform [2]; covered by Daiwa analyst Rick Hsu), 
Ardentec establishes a resilient, differentiated market presence through two structural 
pillars:

• Strategic dual-sourcing anchor and supply chain balancer. As advanced packaging 
and testing capacity is increasingly centralised within leading foundries and mega-
OSATs, tier-1 fabless leaders actively de-risk operations by qualifying secondary 
sources. Ardentec functions as an independent, pure-play testing alternative, providing 
foundry-aligned engineering standards alongside commercial flexibility. This positioning 
allows tier-1 chipmakers to diversify vendor concentration, secure dedicated capacity 
allocations during cyclical tight supply, and mitigate single-point manufacturing 
bottlenecks.

• Technical versatility supported by automotive qualification standards. Ardentec 
maintains a high revenue exposure to automotive and industrial IC testing – sectors that 
demand zero-defect reliability, ultra-wide temperature ranges, and complex mixed-signal 
test protocols. This operational baseline provides significant cross-application versatility. 
During automotive cycle downturns, qualified test cells and probe architectures can be 
reconfigured to support compute, edge AI, and high-frequency communication ICs, 
helping dampen gross margin volatility and stabilising baseline fleet utilisation across 
broader semiconductor cycles.

Ardentec: revenue by product    Ardentec: revenue by application

Source: Company, Daiwa forecasts  Source: Company

Longtan: seven-floor mega-fab to scale AI 
Spanning seven vertical cleanroom floors, the company’s Longtan facility began a multi-
year construction timeline starting in 2026, manufacturing semiconductor chips for tier-1 
foundry customers. Management confirmed Floor 1 achieved commercial mass production 
in 3Q26; its +15% MoM revenue inflection in July validated the expansion. At peak 
utilisation, we estimate each fully loaded floor will generate c.TWD150m per month (TWD 
400-500m quarterly) in revenue. With tooling and equipment installations tracking a 
predictable one-floor-per-quarter cadence, each incremental floor can accommodate a 
maximum of 100 high-end automated test equipment (ATE) platforms.

Commanding an hourly billing rate nearly double that of legacy CP testing (95-100%

sorting from an ancillary segment into Ardentec’s primary growth engine and top-line 
contributor over our forecast horizon.

While Floor 1 capex was self-funded to fast-track qualification, subsequent floor 
expansions are transitioning toward customer-consigned tester models, which will reduce 
balance sheet risk and secure committed wafer allocation. We believe the fleet is custom-
tailored for leading US hyperscaler ASIC roadmaps. By locking in application-specific test 
setups and eliminating idle downtime associated with frequent load-board changeovers, 
Ardentec is able to achieve industry-leading throughput, uncompromised test cell 
efficiency, and maximised asset turns, per management.

Ardentec: capacity expansion    Ardentec: revenue contribution from its Longtan Fab

Proprietary accelerator roadmaps across cloud service providers (CSP) – including AWS 
Trainium/Inferentia, Meta MTIA, and Microsoft Maia – feature starkly heterogeneous probe 
card architectures, thermal docking requirements, and test firmware protocols. We believe 
the modular, multi-story footprint at the company’s Longtan facility provides the physical 
isolation necessary to construct dedicated, IP-secure production cleanrooms for multiple 
hyperscaler customers. As custom AI ASIC testing accounts for a rapidly expanding share 
of the company’s revenue mix relative to legacy automotive exposure, we believe this 
structural diversification serves as a strong catalyst for a rerating for Ardentec towards tier-
1 compute OSAT multiples.

Broad-based UTR inflection on peer capacity spillover 
While automotive and consumer segments navigate cyclical normalisation, Ardentec’s non-
AI capacity is staging a powerful recovery, per management. Based on our channel 
checks, its key OSAT peers (eg, KYEC: 2449 TT, not rated) have aggressively reallocated 
leading-edge test fleets toward mega-cap merchant AI GPUs, creating severe capacity 
bottlenecks for mobile application processor (AP), radio frequency (RF), and networking IC 
designers (such as MediaTek – 2454 TT, TWD4,625, Buy [1], covered by Rick Hsu). 
Therefore, Ardentec is capturing these high-volume, displaced wafer sorting (or chip 
probing, CP) and final test (FT) allocations. This order influx swiftly rebounds mature and 
communication line utilisation rates from trough levels (below 65%) back toward the 80%+ 
threshold, turning legacy capacity into a high-cash-generation baseline with zero asset 
drag.

Semiconductor testing carries a high fixed-cost structure heavily weighted toward 
equipment depreciation and engineering overhead. Historically, once aggregate corporate 
UTR crosses the critical 65% fixed-cost absorption threshold, incremental revenue drops 
directly to the bottom line with minimal variable costs (primarily power and consumables).

Advanced-node ASICs feature extreme sensitivity to thermal dissipation and signal

Next-gen CPO and silicon photonics testing 
Beyond the immediate custom ASIC cycle, Ardentec is securing its next structural growth 
frontier through advanced co-packaged optics (CPO) and silicon photonics (SiPh) wafer-
level testing. As hyperscale AI clusters push copper interconnects to physical transmission 
limits, the industry is transitioning towards optical I/O, which requires testing to shift from 
purely electrical verification to complex electro-optical (E/O) wafer sorting (CP). Unlike 
standard digital logic testing, optical probing demands sub-micron automated fibre 
alignment, precise laser wavelength calibration, optical power loss measurement, and 
specialised thermal-stability testing across photonic integrated circuits (PIC) and electronic 
integrated circuits (EIC) before advanced heterogeneous integration.

Market Analysis 
Structural shift in the IC testing industry 
Reiterating the key message in our Taiwan Testing Interface Initiation: paradigm shift 
accelerated by AI report, we believe the semiconductor testing paradigm is shifting. In the 
multi-die and 2.5D/3D packaging era (eg, TSMC CoWoS, SoIC), wafer testing (chip 
probing, CP) is no longer a commoditised, post-fab defect screening step – it has evolved 
into a mission-critical gating process. We summarise the critical paradigm shift as follows:

• The known good die (KGD) imperative. Heterogeneous integration bundles high-
value compute dies with multiple high bandwidth memory (HBM) stacks. Packaging an 
untested or marginally defective die risks scrapping the entire multi-thousand-dollar 
subsystem. This zero-tolerance threshold elevates CP from sample-based checks to 
exhaustive, full-spec validation across extreme thermal ranges.

• Structural Test-Time Inflation (2-3x). High reticle-limit AI/HPC custom silicon, 
expanding power envelopes (>700W), and thousands of high-speed interconnect 
channels have doubled or tripled test times per wafer. Consequently, automated test 
equipment (ATE) fleet demand is decoupling from raw silicon unit growth, driven instead 
by compounding tester hours.

• Next-Gen CPO Frontier. Rapid silicon tape-out cadences demand high-density vertical 
probe cards (VPC) and micro-cantilever interfaces supporting parallel multi-site testing. 
Beyond electrical testing, the emergence of CPO and SiPh requires active sub-micron 
optical alignment and electro-optical (E/O) sorting, creating multi-year technical barriers 
and pricing premiums for early movers.

Market dynamics: testing outperforms packaging 
According to Gartner (Semiconductor Assembly and Test Services, Worldwide, Sep 2025, 
Semiconductors and Electronics Team), total package and test market size is projected to 
increase from USD47.3bn to USD65.2bn over 2025-29E, representing an 8.4% CAGR 
over the period. Given that third-party market data typically blends packaging and testing 
into total OSAT, we granularly disaggregate historical revenue across major US and Taiwan 
vendors.

While consumer electronics endured a prolonged post-pandemic inventory correction over 
2022-25, the emergence of AI/HPC workloads created a pronounced divergence across 
the backend: historical industry data indicates that the testing sub-segment delivered 
materially higher year-over-year revenue growth than packaging over 2023-25, propelled 
by multi-die KGD mandates and structural test-time inflation.

Advantage of pure-play testing 
We think three reasons distinguish dedicated testing pure-plays from traditional integrated 
OSATs:

• Asset-light model and lean working capital mechanics. Integrated OSATs face 
substantial working capital exposure to expensive ABF substrates, precious metal 
bonding wires, and carrier materials. In contrast, pure-play testing carries virtually zero 
direct material inventory, insulating balance sheets from write-down risks. Furthermore, 
automated test equipment depreciation is concentrated directly within COGS, with 
capital intensity effectively moderated by customer-consigned tester allocations.

Global OSAT: Capex intensity

Source: Bloomberg

• Fleet flexibility and potential spillover orders. Unlike specialised packaging lines that 
require extensive physical retooling, standardised high-end ATE platforms exhibit 
exceptional fleet flexibility. Once test programs and interface hardware are qualified, 
testers can rapidly transition across diverse application domains – from premium mobile 
APs and automotive MCUs to complex custom ASICs – by swapping application-
specific load boards and high-density probe cards. As tier-1 OSATs concentrate their 
tester fleets on merchant AI GPU allocations, mobile AP, 5G RF, and high-speed 
networking chipmakers face severe capacity displacement. We believe pure-play test 
houses could benefit from a dual growth driver: rising demand for high-margin AI/HPC 
programs and incremental mobile and networking orders redirected to underutilised 
legacy tester capacity. This dynamic could decisively shift commercial bargaining 
leverage to pure testers, expanding hourly billing rates and unlocking structural gross 
margin leverage.

• IP neutrality and ecosystem balancing. North American hyperscalers designing 
proprietary custom silicon actively avoid monolithic vendor lock-in and potential IP 
conflicts within integrated supply chains. Pure-play testers provide a strictly neutral 
counterweight with uncompromised test cell isolation. Multi-story modular facilities

run dedicated engineering cells, allowing pure-play test houses to function as 
indispensable, IP-secure manufacturing partners across the advanced foundry 
ecosystem.

Financial analysis 
Revenue growth in 2026-28E 
We forecast Ardentec’s top-line to enter a multi-year expansion cycle, accelerating from 
TWD14.0bn in 2025 to TWD19.5bn in 2026E (+39.0% YoY), TWD26.8bn in 2027E 
(+37.5% YoY), and reaching TWD34.4bn in 2028E (+28.2% YoY). This represents a 3-year 
revenue CAGR of +34.8% (2025-28E), driven by a powerful confluence of volume 
expansion and structural pricing power across both advanced and mature test fleets.

First, we believe the orderly floor-by-floor commissioning of the 7-story Longtan facility 
delivers a predictable volume baseline, with each fully loaded cleanroom floor contributing 
c.TWD150m per month (c.TWD450m+ quarterly) in incremental run-rate revenue. Beyond 
pure wafer throughput, we expect revenue quality to see a significant mix upgrade, as 
advanced wafer sorting for hyperscaler AI ASICs and complex HPC processors command 
an hourly billing rate of nearly double (95-100% premium) that of traditional automotive and 
industrial IC testing, fundamentally elevating revenue density per tester hour.

Furthermore, as Ardentec prioritises engineering bandwidth, cleanroom footprint, and 
tester allocations toward high-margin advanced CP, legacy and mature-node test capacity 
faces internal supply tightness. This self-induced capacity crowding shifts pricing leverage 
back to Ardentec, allowing the company to enact upward price adjustments across lagging-
node test services and accelerating a broad-based, corporate-wide blended ASP 
expansion.

Gross margin inflection driven by UTR surge  
We believe capacity utilisation rate serves as the single most critical determinant of 
Ardentec’s gross margin trajectory. Over the coming quarters, we project a structural 
rebound in corporate-wide utilisation driven by 2 powerful operational forces.

First, the rapid ramp of the Longtan advanced testing fab—operating at an optimal 85-90% 
UTR ceiling—will represent a rapidly expanding proportion of total capacity, immediately 
enriching the blended margin profile. Second, incoming spillover orders from tier-1 
communications and mobile AP clients are directly refilling legacy and mature testing lines. 
Because these mature tools are almost or already fully depreciated, incremental spillover 
revenue incurs virtually zero depreciation burden, generating exceptionally high operating 
leverage and outsized gross profit contribution, in our view.

Therefore, we estimate that this dual dynamic of high-end capacity scaling and fully 
amortised tool revitalisation will propel gross margins from 36.3% in 2025 to 42.3% in 
2026E, 44.5% in 2027E and reach 45.0% in 2028E.

Ardentec: gross margin

Source: Company, Daiwa forecasts

Earnings led by gross margin amid subdued operating 
leverage 
We believe that Ardentec’s earnings inflection is predominantly a story of gross margin and 
operating leverage rather than structural opex dilution. The high-fixed-cost nature of the 
wafer testing business—governed by multi-billion-dollar ATE depreciation and cleanroom 
overhead—is heavily concentrated within Cost of Goods Sold (COGS), per management. 
Consequently, the powerful fixed-cost absorption resulting from Longtan’s ramp and peer 
spillover orders directly fuels gross margin expansion, while operating leverage at the 
SG&A/opex level remains comparatively subdued.

Because high-end ASIC and electro-optical testing require tailored test program 
development, application-specific load board debugging and dedicated test engineering 
headcount for each CSP roadmap, we believe R&D and engineering talent function as 
quasi-variable expenses that scale in tandem with incremental floor additions. As a result, 
we project Ardentec’s opex-to-sales ratio to remain relatively stable in the 9-10% corridor 
over 2026-28E.

Balance sheet and cash flow 
While management has not provided official guidance due to dynamic cleanroom 
construction milestones and equipment lead-time variations, we model an orderly 
deployment cadence of one cleanroom floor per quarter at the Longtan mega-facility. 
Under this baseline, we forecast total capital expenditures (capex) to step up aggressively 
to TWD14.5bn in 2026E and TWD18.5bn in 2027E to support facility buildout and early tool 
installations.

To fund this expansion phase, Ardentec intends to prioritise low-cost bank borrowings over 
issuing overseas or domestic convertible bonds (ECB/CB), deliberately avoiding equity 
dilution to maximise EPS accretion during the upcoming earnings supercycle. 
Concurrently, management plans to optimise capital allocation by pragmatically calibrating 
its historical cash dividend pay-out ratio. We estimate the pay-out ratio will moderate 
slightly from 70% to 50% to retain internal cash for high-return AI capacity. Meanwhile, we 
believe the company actively negotiates customer-consigned tester models for subsequent 
cleanroom floors. This is a framework that insulates the cost structure from severe, front-
loaded depreciation burdens and channels capital directly into superior return on equity 
(ROE) growth.

Benefitting from disciplined financing, high asset turnover on advanced wafer sort lines and 
gross margin expansion, we project Ardentec's ROE to stage a structural recovery from the 
cyclical trough experienced during the 2023 automotive downturn, steadily increasing from 
15.1% to 32.1% over 2025-2027E.

Valuation and recommendation 
Initiating coverage with a Buy (1) rating 
Given the current structural mix transition from cyclical automotives towards high-margin 
AI/HPC custom ASICs, amplified gross margin and operating leverage from the Longtan 
ramp, and ROE inflection likely to surpass its 2022 historical peak of c.23% over 2026-
28E, we initiate coverage of Ardentec with a Buy (1) rating and 12-month TP of TWD340, 
based on a target PER of 25.0x applied to our 4-quarter-forward EPS. Our target multiple 
of 25.0x is supported by a 48% EPS CAGR over 2025-28E (PEG of c.0.52x).

Historically, Ardentec traded within a compressed band of 10-25x forward PER due to its 
cyclical automotive and industrial exposure. While the stock has begun to re-rate alongside 
recent EPS upgrades, we view this multiple expansion as far from complete. In addition, 
we believe Ardentec still trades at a noticeable discount (14.9x PER on 2027E EPS) vs. 
leading AI testing peers (KYEC trading at 18.7x PER, while ASE at 26.4x), leaving ample 
room for multiple expansion as its pure-play test economics and earnings growth outpace 
the broader backend sector.

Ardentec (3264 TT): 9 September 2026 
Risks to our call 
1. Delays in capacity expansion (primary risk). Delays in Longtan cleanroom and 
equipment installations, or customer qualifications could disrupt the floor-by-floor ramp, 
deferring high-margin hyperscaler ASIC revenue and diluting near-term gross margin 
leverage.  
2. Pricing pressure as a second-source supplier (secondary risk). Serving as a 
second-source supplier forces Ardentec to accept lower hourly rates than primary 
competitors. Furthermore, non-AI clients demand annual price cuts, limiting gross 
margin recovery unless capacity utilisation remains exceptionally high.  
3. Slow automotive and industrial recovery (secondary risk). Prolonged inventory 
adjustments in automotive and industrial markets continue to drag down IDM revenue 
share. Clients are placing short-term urgent orders rather than rebuilding long-term 
inventory, creating demand uncertainty for mature testing capacity.

Ardentec (3264 TT): 9 September 2026 
Appendix 
Company introduction 
Founded in 1999 and headquartered in Hsinchu, Ardentec is an independent 
semiconductor testing service provider. The company specialises in wafer testing (wafer 
sort) and final testing for memory, logic and mixed-signal integrated circuits. Its diverse 
portfolio addresses several sectors, including automotive electronics, 5G communications, 
storage and advanced AI/HPC ASICs.

Through strategic investments in Giga Solution and Raytek, Ardentec has also successfully 
expanded into RF testing and bumping capabilities. Its global customer base spans world-
class foundries, IDMs and fabless designers, such as MediaTek, Marvell, Texas 
Instruments, Infineon and NXP.

Ardentec’s core competitive advantage lies in its early leadership in automotive 
semiconductor testing, underpinned by ISO 26262 certification and stringent reliability 
standards that support strong customer stickiness and order stability. As an independent, 
pure-play testing provider, Ardentec serves as a neutral strategic partner to leading fabless 
companies, offering foundry-grade engineering capabilities, dedicated capacity and greater 
commercial flexibility.

Its role extends beyond that of a conventional second-source supplier: by providing an 
independent alternative to increasingly consolidated foundry and OSAT ecosystems, 
Ardentec helps customers diversify supply-chain risk, secure critical testing capacity and 
avoid potential bottlenecks. Backed by its state-of-the-art Longtan facility dedicated to 
advanced AI ASIC testing and a global manufacturing footprint across Taiwan, Nanjing, 
South Korea and Singapore, Ardentec is well positioned as an indispensable testing 
partner for tier-1 and emerging semiconductor customers.

Shareholder structure 
Ardentec’s shareholder base is well diversified, with no single controlling shareholder. 
Dresdner Bank AG is the largest holder with an 8.36% stake, followed by Macronix 
International (7.33%) and Vanguard Group (4.66%). The register also includes long-term 
institutional investors such as BlackRock, Dimensional Fund Advisors, BNP Paribas and 
Taiwan’s pension-related funds, providing a stable ownership structure and supporting 
governance transparency.

Taiwan Industrials

What’s new: Eternal Precision Mechanics (EPM) reported its August 2026 
revenue after market hours on 9 September 2026.

What’s the impact: August revenue beat expectations. EPM reported 
August 2026 revenue of TWD359.8m, up 95.7% MoM and 111.5% YoY. 
QTD revenue reached 88.4% of our previous 3Q26 forecast and 74.2% of 
the Bloomberg consensus. Given the faster-than-expected revenue 
recognition schedule and a sharp increase in recognised high-end 
equipment units, which should drive a more favourable product mix, we 
raise our 3Q26 revenue forecast by 33% to TWD972.7m, gross margin by 
3.1ppts to 48.5%, and EPS by 92% to TWD1.86.

Vacuum laminators are emerging as the next ABF bottleneck. Despite 
a partial conversion of backlog into revenue in August, EPM’s backlog 
continued to increase from TWD810m at end-July to TWD880m in early 
September. With lead times extending further to 36 months, vacuum 
laminators are emerging as the next bottleneck in the ABF capacity 
expansion cycle. Given the robust demand from ABF substrate makers, we 
see upside potential to EPM’s capacity expansion plans. On margins, we 
expect continued product-mix improvement and the full realisation of price 
increases to lift gross margin by 6.6ppts/1.3ppts YoY to 53.2%/54.5% in 
2027/28E, driving a 2026-28E EPS CAGR of 141%.

Moulding film adoption opens a new growth avenue. Traditional 
transfer and compression moulding typically use granular, powder, or liquid-
type compounds for encapsulation. During our visit to SEMICON, Japanese 
material suppliers Nagase (8012 JP, JPY1,150.5, Outperform [2]; covered 
by Masayuki Nagano) and Resonac (4004 JP, JPY16,070, Outperform [2]; 
covered by Hidemitsu Umebayashi) noted growing customer interest in 
moulding films. These offer better filling performance, better warpage 
control and higher flowability. This makes them increasingly suitable for 
advanced packaging applications such as panel level packaging and 
component-embedded substrates. EPM supplies moulding-film laminators 
for both applications, with revenue contribution expected to begin in 2027.

What we recommend: We lift our 2026-28E EPS by 22-26% to reflect the 
full realisation of price increases and improving product mix. We reaffirm 
our Buy (1) rating and raise our 12-month TP to TWD720 (from TWD600) 
based on an unchanged target PER of 40x, applied to our 1-year forward 
EPS forecast. Key downside risk: slower-than-expected substrate capex 
growth.

How we differ: We likely conduct a more comprehensive analysis than 
others on ABF industry demand and moulding film development.

Company profile 
Eternal was established in 2022 through the spin-off of Eternal Material’s equipment division and its 
subsequent merger with Nikko-Materials, a wholly owned Japanese subsidiary. The company was listed 
in January 2026 and is the global leader in IC substrate vacuum laminators, serving all major substrate 
manufacturers worldwide.

ESG risks
Risks Management Analyst comments
G
Executive/board
quality 1
Eternal demonstrates a solid corporate governance structure supported by a balanced and
diversified board composition. The company’sboard consists of 7 members, including 3
independent directors, with backgrounds spanning industry operations, finance, accounting,
legal, and academia, enabling comprehensive oversight across business and governance
functions.
Capital management 2
Eternal adopts a prudent capital management strategy, supported by a stable shareholder
structure and disciplined financial policy. The company is majority-owned by Eternal Materials
(over 60% stake), providing long-term strategic backing and financial stability.
Related party &
transaction 1
Eternal discloses related-party transactions transparently and enforces strict governance
procedures to manage potential conflicts of interest. Board members are required to recuse
themselves from discussions and voting on matters involving personal or affiliated interests,
such as asset acquisitions, patent licensing, and remuneration decisions.
S Product quality &
safety 1
Eternal maintains strict product quality control, covering design, manufacturing, and delivery
processes. The company emphasizes equipment reliability and performance stability, supported
by long-term client relationships and low defect risks, ensuring high customer satisfaction and
consistent product safety standards.
E Product design &
lifecycle management 2
Eternal focuses on enhancing product durability and energy efficiency through continuous R&D
innovation. Its equipment design emphasizes precision, extended lifecycle and reduced material
waste, aligning product development with resource efficiency and long-term environmental
sustainability goals.

Industry View In-Line
Our CY26 full-year forecast is now at 80-85K racks: This year is a strong one for
downstream rack assembly. We expect over 100% y/y growth in rack shipments, vs.

~26.5k last year.
Quanta (2382.TW, OW): August revenue was NT$424.0B (+16% m/m, +177% y/y).
We attribute the m/m growth mainly to higher GB200/300 rack shipments at 2.5-
2.55K racks (+22% m/m), despite offset slightly by lower NB shipments at 2.6M
units (-7% m/m, -37% y/y). Combining July and August GB200/300 rack shipments,
Quanta has already shipped ~4.6K racks, which would imply upside to our current
3Q forecast of ~6.4K racks. We think there is likely also upside to consensus

forecast, since combined July+August revenue reached ~NT$790B, which is 81% of
MSe and 71% of consensus 3Q revenue estimates. This also implies that there could
be upside to our full-year estimate of ~18.7K racks.
Wistron (3231.TW, OW): August revenue was  NT$460.1B (+49% m/m, +166% y/y).
We attribute the m/m growth to: 1) materially higher GB200/300 server computing
tray shipments  (2.3-2.4K rack equivalents, by our estimates, up approximately 100%

m/m), and higher Wiwynn revenue at ~NT$144.3B (+23% m/m, +50% y/y), while
offset by lower NB shipments at 1.4M units (-13% m/m, -36% y/y), lower DT
shipments at 500K (-29% m/m, -38% y/y) and lower monitor shipments at 750K (-
17% m/m, -6% y/y). Combined July + August revenue reached ~NT$768.3B, which is
74% of MSe and 75% of consensus 3Q revenue estimate, implying upside to 3Q. This
also implies that there could be upside to our full-year forecast of ~17.9K racks.

Hon Hai (2317.TW, OW): August revenue was NT$921.8B (-3% m/m, +52% y/y), with
server-related revenue seeing the strongest m/m growth, followed by components
and other products, while computing products and consumer segment, which mainly
includes iPhone assembly, declined m/m. We model HH's GB rack shipments at 2.6K
racks (+6% m/m). Our full-year forecast is unchanged, at ~31.7K racks.
Morgan Stanley does and seeks to do business with
companies covered in Morgan Stanley Research. As a result,

communications with a subject company, public appearances
and trading securities held by a research analyst account.
Key Takeaways
We estimate GB200/300 rack output in August at ~8.4K (+27% m/m), within
which:
Quanta shipped 2.5-2.55K  GB200/GB300 racks.
Wistron shipped 2.3-2.4K GB200/GB300 racks.
Hon Hai shipped ~2.6K GB200/300 racks.

Valuation Methodology and Risks
Hon Hai Precision (2317.TW)
Base case scenario value, derived from a residual income valuation model. Our key assump-
tions include a cost of equity of 8.5%, a medium-term growth rate of 13%, and a terminal
growth rate of 3%.
Risks to Upside
n Better-than-expected iPhone sell-through
n Faster progress in AI server business
n Faster EV business development progress
n Any new M&A activity that could improve sentiment

Risks to Downside
n Lower iPhone sell-through
n Smaller profit contribution from AI business
n Slower EV business development progress
n Geopolitical developments that could negatively affect foreign investment
Quanta Computer Inc. (2382.TW)
Base case, residual income model. Key assumptions include a cost of equity of 9.0% (beta of
1.2, equity premium of 6.0% and risk-free rate of 1.5%), an 8.5% medium-term growth rate, and
a 3% terminal growth rate.

Risks to Upside
n Stronger-than-expected NB demand
n Stronger-than-expected Apple Watch demand
n Stronger-than-expected server demand
n Faster-than-expected AI server penetration
Risks to Downside
n Weaker-than-expected NB demand
n Softer-than-expected Apple Watch demand
n Weak margin performance owing to rising labor costs and sales shortfalls
n Fierce price competition in the mega data center segment
n Slower-than-expected AI server penetration

Wistron Corporation (3231.TW)
Base case, residual income valuation. Key assumptions: 8.7% cost of equity, 7.0% medium-
term growth rate and 3% terminal growth rate.
Risks to Upside
n Faster-than-expected divestiture of consumer electronics business
n Stronger-than-expected NB demand
n Margin expansion from better product mix

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: (1) Cooling: the new iPhone is embedded with a more 
powerful SoC (A20 Pro) and Apple Intelligence, making thermal management essential 
to the device. The next generation of Vapor Chamber is used in the new iPhones, which 
we see as positive for the cooling suppliers. Read more: AVC, AAC; (2) Camera: variable 
aperture is adopted in rear cameras, in which lens aperture changes based on the focal 
length, allowing easier user control of DoF (depth of field), taking pictures in low lighting, 
or having a more natural broken gradient background when in portrait mode. Read 
more: Largan. Selling price is higher by US$100 (or high single-digit %) compared to 
iPhone 17 Pro series, with the same delivery time.  
Apple Watch and Airpods: Airpods 5 feature active noise cancellation, and are 
designed to allow more natural interaction (e.g. transparency mode, better conversation 
awareness). The wireless charging case models are US$30 cheaper compared to Airpods 
4. Apple Watch 12 and Ultra 4 are priced the same as the previous generation with

## Document 098: 260910_gs_TSMC

Source PDF: all report pdf/260910_gs_TSMC.pdf
Report source: line報告備份
Date: 2026-09-10
Pages: 10
Extraction status: ok

### Page 1

Presenters: Wendell Huang, SVP & CFO  
Bottom Line: We have three key takeaways: (1) TSMC continues to view AI as a 
multi-year megatrend that remains at a very early stage, with lower compute costs 
expected to accelerate AI adoption and ultimately drive greater demand for 
advanced silicon; (2) execution in Arizona continues to progress well, with Phase 1 
achieving yields comparable to Taiwan and already generating profits, while TSMC 
expects approximately 30% of its N2-and-beyond capacity to be located outside 
Taiwan in five years, primarily in Arizona; and (3) despite dilution from the N2 ramp 
and overseas expansion, management remains comfortable achieving its long-term 
gross margin target of 56% and above, supported by disciplined capacity planning, 
high utilization, productivity improvements, cost reductions, and pricing that reflects 
TSMC’s value. 
Key Takeaways

AI remains in the early stages of a multi-year megatrend: TSMC continues to n
see increasing adoption of AI. Management also highlighted the shift from 
generative AI toward agentic AI, which should broaden compute demand 
beyond accelerators to CPUs. TSMC remains confident in the durability of the AI 
cycle based on discussions not only with its direct customers but also with its 
customers’ customers. Recent visits of US CSPs further reinforced management’s 
confidence, as cloud service providers appeared well prepared in areas including 
power and broader infrastructure deployment. 
Lower compute costs should drive greater consumption and silicon demand: n
Management believes open-source models and continued improvements in 
computing efficiency will reduce token costs, leading to greater AI 
consumption and broader adoption, supporting incremental demand for 
advanced silicon. TSMC has already incorporated this dynamic into its capacity 
planning and continues to expand aggressively to support what it views as

### Page 2

structural, multi-year demand growth.
Disciplined demand validation remains critical amid aggressive expansion: n
TSMC uses a combination of top-down and bottom-up analysis to validate demand.
Its top-down assessment considers macroeconomic conditions, semiconductor
demand, fabless/system companies, the foundry industry, etc, while its bottom-up
approach evaluates demand across different segments and incorporates feedback
from customers and customers’ customers. Management acknowledged that

semiconductors will remain cyclical, but believes correctly identifying the underlying
megatrend is more important than attempting to forecast every short-term
fluctuation.
Arizona execution is demonstrating that TSMC’s manufacturing model can n
travel: TSMC reiterated that overseas expansion is based on customer demand for
geographic flexibility and an appropriate level of government support. Arizona
Phase 1, using N4 technology, is in operation, with yields comparable to Taiwan,

satisfactory quality and reliability, and positive profitability. Management views
this as an important milestone because it demonstrates internally and to customers
that TSMC can produce wafers in the US with the same quality as in Taiwan.
Equipment move-in for Phase 2, which will use N3 technology, is expected to begin
soon; construction of Phase 3 has started; and preparation work for Phase 4 and the
first US advanced-packaging facility is underway.

Arizona has substantial room for further expansion: In addition to its original n
Arizona development, TSMC has acquired another parcel of land capable of
accommodating an additional five to six fabs, supporting its recently
announced incremental US$100bn investment. Based on its current plan, TSMC
expects approximately 30% of its N2-and-beyond capacity to be located outside
Taiwan in five years, primarily in Arizona. However, the most advanced technologies

will continue to ramp first in Taiwan because the early-stage technology transfer
requires close collaboration and frequent movement of engineers among R&D and
manufacturing sites. Overseas deployment will generally follow after the technology
has stabilized in Taiwan.
Customers increasingly value and are willing to pay for geographic flexibility: n
Management noted that customers initially requested only a modest amount of
geographically diversified supply, but their requirements have increased as TSMC has

demonstrated successful execution in Arizona. TSMC believes this geographic
flexibility represents incremental value and intends to reflect that value in its pricing,
with customers increasingly willing to recognize the associated premium.
Technology, manufacturing excellence, capacity, and trust underpin TSMC’s n
competitive moat: Management believes customers select a foundry partner based
on access to the best technology, the ability to ramp rapidly into high-volume

manufacturing with attractive economics, sufficient capacity, and confidence that
the foundry will not compete with its customers. TSMC is confident in maintaining
this lead by continuing to advance its roadmap. Management also highlighted its
record of rapidly ramping new technologies, the scale of its wafer and
advanced-packaging investments, and its consistent delivery against customer
10 September 2026   2
Goldman Sachs TSMC (2330.TW)For the exclusive use of KEVINLU@LENOVO.COM

e92c7a75ab8b4efbba794e6b187208c8

### Page 3

commitments as key elements of customer trust that cannot be replicated through
CapEx or engineering recruitment alone.
Pricing remains strategic rather than opportunistic: TSMC does not intend to raise n
prices simply because near-term utilization is high, nor reduce prices simply because
utilization temporarily weakens. Instead, the company’s approach is to price
sustainably and consistently based on the value it provides, while ensuring that
customers can remain successful over the long term. Management noted that

TSMC’s structural profitability has continued to improve, with its long-term gross
margin target increasing from 50% five years ago to 53% and now 56% and above.
Leading-edge wafer and advanced-packaging capacity remain tight: n
Management continues to build capacity wherever possible to meet customer
demand. N3 demand remains particularly strong: unlike prior technology cycles,
when demand for a node typically began declining two to three years after its

introduction, TSMC is adding further N3 capacity and still does not expect supply
to be sufficient. The company is also expanding advanced-packaging capacity to
address strong accelerator demand. Outside TSMC, management identified power
and memory as potential bottlenecks cited by other parts of the AI supply chain,
while emphasizing that foundry capacity itself remains difficult to expand because
fabs require two to three years to build and another one to two years to ramp.

TSMC’s disclosed AI revenue understates its broader exposure: Management n
reiterated that its disclosed AI revenue definition is relatively narrow and primarily
captures GPUs, custom AI accelerators and memory base die. It excludes CPUs and
networking products because TSMC cannot reliably determine whether each chip is
ultimately deployed in an AI system. As agentic AI drives incremental demand across
x86, Arm, and RISC-V CPUs, as well as networking and other supporting silicon,

TSMC’s total AI-related exposure is therefore broader than its reported
AI-accelerator revenue. The company intends to retain its existing definition until it
can more accurately distinguish the end use of these products.
No visible barrier to continued transistor scaling: TSMC is currently ramping N2, n
with A14 expected approximately two years later, while development of the
subsequent node is already underway. Management does not currently see a

technical issue preventing delivery of the next node or continued advancement
beyond the existing roadmap. TSMC views close collaboration with customers as a
key foundry advantage, allowing the company to develop each technology against
specific customer performance, power, density, and economic requirements.
Cross-node capacity optimization is an underappreciated advantage: TSMC n
highlighted its ability to generate additional output through productivity

improvements and to convert tools and capacity across technology nodes. For
example, the company can use portions of its N5 capacity to support N3 demand
and can also optimize capacity across less-adjacent nodes where technically
feasible. Management views this cross-node flexibility as a distinctive element of
TSMC’s manufacturing excellence, allowing the company to respond more
quickly to demand changes while reducing the risk of capacity obsolescence.

Advanced packaging is strategic primarily because it enables wafer growth: n
10 September 2026   3
Goldman Sachs TSMC (2330.TW)For the exclusive use of KEVINLU@LENOVO.COM
e92c7a75ab8b4efbba794e6b187208c8

### Page 4

CoWoS capacity remains tight, and TSMC already started outsourcing selected 
packaging processes to OSAT partners to support additional growth. Management 
emphasized that advanced packaging is intended primarily to ensure and enable 
wafer demand rather than serve as a standalone profit pool. TSMC is therefore 
developing multiple packaging architectures, including panel-level packaging, etc, 
while remaining open to customers using alternative packaging providers, as either 
approach ultimately supports demand for TSMC wafers. 
Advanced-packaging execution remains a key differentiator: TSMC noted that its n
current advanced-packaging capability supports approximately 5.5x reticle size, 
with a roadmap to reach approximately 14x reticle sizes within the next several 
years. While competing roadmaps may also appear attractive, management believes 
execution and the ability to deliver in high-volume manufacturing will ultimately 
determine competitive outcomes. TSMC does not believe competitors can use 
advanced-packaging wins to meaningfully displace its leading-edge wafer 
business, as foundry and packaging remain fundamentally different businesses. 
A unified TSMC culture supports overseas manufacturing execution: TSMC’s n
objective is not to create separate Taiwan and US cultures, but to establish a 
consistent TSMC culture centered on integrity, commitment, innovation, and 
customer trust (ICIC). Locally hired Arizona employees spend six to eighteen months 
training and working in Taiwan, while experienced Taiwan-based employees are 
assigned to Arizona to work alongside local teams. Over time, the number of Taiwan 
assignees should decline as locally trained employees assume greater responsibility. 
TSMC is applying this approach across its overseas manufacturing sites. 
Management remains comfortable with its 56%-and-above long-term gross n
margin target: TSMC reiterated its 6 major drivers of profitability: new-technology 
ramp, pricing, cost, product mix, utilization, and FX. The N2 ramp is expected to 
dilute 2026 GM by approximately 2-3ppts, but its profitability should improve over 
time toward the corporate average; management also noted that N2’s structural 
profitability is better than N3 at a comparable stage. Overseas expansion is 
expected to dilute GM by 2-3ppts during the early portion of the current five-year 
period, then widening to 3-ppts later as more overseas fabs begin production. Each 
new fab will initially create dilution before improving along its learning curve. Taking 
these puts and takes together, management remains very comfortable that 
disciplined capacity planning, healthy utilization, cost reduction, productivity 
gains, and pricing that reflects TSMC’s value will enable the company to deliver 
for shareholders and achieve its long-term gross margin target ‘of 56% and 
higher’ with focus on the ‘higher’ side.

Industry View In-Line
AI-driven specification upgrades are reshaping the economics of copper-clad
laminate (CCL), the core material in PCBs, and driving demand for higher-

performance copper foil and glass cloth. We expect the global CCL TAM to rise
from US$19B in 2025 to US$47B by 2030, implying a 20% CAGR (vs market
expectations at US$35-40B), with AI/data-center applications accounting for 90%
of incremental growth and nearly two-thirds of demand by decade-end.
Content, not units, is the key growth driver. We estimate rising material intensity
accounts for 84% of AI-related CCL growth, as next-generation compute and

networking platforms move to higher-layer-count PCBs, lower-loss CCL and
smoother HVLP copper foil. Our bottom-up model implies the HVLP4 market
grows from <US$50M in 2025 to US$2.8B by 2030, a 123% CAGR. Extending the
same framework further downstream, we forecast the global PCB TAM will rise
from US$58bn to US$135bn over 2025–30, an 18% CAGR.
Broadening the AI trade upstream. We think high-end CCL, HVLP copper foil and
advanced glass cloth have entered an earnings upcycle but have yet to reach full

earnings realization and peak-cycle conditions. AI-driven specification upgrades are
reducing the number of  qualified suppliers and supporting mix, pricing and margins,
while long qualification cycles, lower yields and equipment bottlenecks should slow
the supply response.
Morgan Stanley does and seeks to do business with
companies covered in Morgan Stanley Research. As a result,
investors should be aware that the firm may have a conflict of
interest that could affect the objectivity of Morgan Stanley

communications with a subject company, public appearances
and trading securities held by a research analyst account.
Key Takeaways
Long qualification cycles and lower production yields in advanced copper foil and
glass cloth should keep effective high-end CCL supply tight into 2028.
Our proprietary bottom-up analysis quantifies copper foil, CCL and PCB content
across Nvidia, AMD, TPU and Trainium platforms.
We introduce a scorecard comparing 16 PCB, substrate & materials suppliers on

six factors to distinguish structural winners from cyclical beneficiaries.
DDR4-like supply squeeze; standard E-glass pricing likely has further upside as
capacity shifts toward higher-value, more advanced grade cloth.
Initiate at OW on EMC (NT$8,400 PT), TUC (NT$2,700 PT), Co-Tech (NT$730
PT), and KB Laminates (HK$75 PT).

Executive Summary
Why read this report?
We provide a comprehensive understanding of what copper foil, and copper-clad
laminates are and how they fit into the PCB supply chain. In addition, we have built
a proprietary bottom-up model to model out the copper foil and copper-clad
laminates market (please reach out to us for the model).
We also broke down the copper foil, copper-clad laminate, and printed circuit
board content per AI system across the different Nvidia, AMD, TPU, and Trainium

architectures.
AI has completely overhauled the PCB supply chain, going all the way up to upstream
materials like CCL (key raw material used in PCB production), copper foil (used in CCL
production), as well as electronic glass cloth (used in CCL production) and others. ABF
substrates are also seeing similar tailwinds, but we have talked about that here, here, and
here. In this report, we focus primarily on CCL and copper foil, but also touch on glass

cloth.
We forecast the CCL market to grow at a 20% CAGR over 2025-30, to US$47B from
US$19B (2.5x). Unit and content growth both contribute. AI data center cluster
deployments lift volumes, while faster signal transmission speeds require upgraded CCL
to contain insertion loss and crosstalk, on top of a mix shift toward higher layer-count and
more complex PCBs.
Against this demand, we see high-end CCL as under-supplied. Only a handful of suppliers

globally are qualified for M8+ grades, including EMC, Panasonic, TUC, Doosan, and
Shengyi. Because CCL capacity is grade-agnostic in architecture, nameplate capacity
overstates effective high-grade supply, and M7/M8+ supply-demand is therefore difficult
to quantify with precision. The absence of a precise gap does not change the direction. We
expect high-end tightness to translate into firmer pricing and margin expansion for the
qualified incumbents.

In copper foil, we forecast the high-end HVLP4 market to reach US$2.8B by 2030, a
123% CAGR over 2025-2030, though off a de minimis base. HVLP4 (hyper very low
profile) foil is the enabling input for low-loss, high-speed CCL, and therefore a gating item
in the AI PCB supply chain.
Effective capacity rests with five suppliers today: Mitsui Kinzoku, Co-Tech, Furukawa,
Fukuda and Copper Foil Luxembourg at roughly 1,000t/month, with Mitsui alone at 41%

of 2026 capacity. Adding to that base is harder than nameplate suggests. Converting
HVLP2 lines is not one-for-one; the longer production cycle cuts effective output by  more
than 40%. New lines require 6-12 months to ramp, and sit behind delivery queues for
surface-treatment equipment concentrated among a small number of Japanese suppliers.
We model demand rising to 39.2kt in 2027 from 12.3kt in 2026 (+218% y/y), and further
growing to 52.0kt in 2028 (+33% y/y). That would leave the market in a deficit of 31% by

### Page 5

M
Foundation
Morgan Stanley Research 5
2027 and 20% by 2028. As such, we expect a handful of qualified producers to hold
meaningful pricing power over that window.
Our conclusion is that CCL makers that are able to secure the full input set of cloth, foil
and resin should hold pricing power over downstream customers.
As a result of our bottom-up analysis of CCL and its upstream materials, we expect the
PCB TAM to grow from US$58B in 2025 to US$135B by 2030, representing an 18%

CAGR.
Beyond discovery: Why high-end CCL stocks still have room
to run
We believe the market continues to underestimate the extent to which AI
infrastructure investment will expand end demand for copper-clad laminate. Our 2030
CCL total addressable market estimate of US$47B is meaningfully above market forecasts
of US$35-40B.
The key difference lies not only in our assumptions for AI server and data-center unit
growth, but also in the increasing material intensity of next-generation computing and

networking platforms. Higher layer counts, larger and more complex PCBs, faster data-
transmission requirements, and the growing use of premium low-loss and high-speed
materials should drive CCL content per system materially higher. This is all made possible
with more advanced copper foil  with tighter surface-profile, signal-integrity, and reliability
requirements.
Structural demand is supported by capex. The spending backdrop still has more than a

year of visible growth in it. Our  house view on cash cloud capex now stands at US$1.2T in
2026 (+104% y/y) and US$1.6T  in 2027 (+38% y/y) vs. consensus at US$1.39T for 2027.
This compares with buyside expectations of US$1.8T+ (including financial and operating
leases), suggesting there could still be meaningful room for further upward consensus
revisions.
CCL content is growing faster than AI-system units. The demand driver is a specification
ladder, not a single product cycle, and that distinction is what makes the cycle durable.

Layer counts on AI server motherboards are increasing with each generation to support
additional routing space for more signals as AI boards become more complex, while rising
signal and thermal demands also support the adoption of higher grade CCLs. Crucially,
each rung multiplies rather than adds, because moving up a grade changes the resin
chemistry, the copper-foil profile and the glass-cloth grade simultaneously. Content per
rack can therefore keep rising even if unit shipment growth moderates. The continuing

migration toward lower-loss grades is another reason the earnings opportunity may have
further to run.

The real scarcity is qualified, high-yield capacity. High-speed laminate is not a
commodity that can be replaced solely on price; materials must be validated for signal

loss, thermal reliability, dimensional stability and compatibility with specific PCB
fabrication processes. For example, an upgrade to M8 grade CCL is not a simple
incremental upgrade from M7. It requires simultaneous improvements in low-loss resin,
smoother HVLP copper foil, higher-spec low-Dk glass cloth, and much tighter
manufacturing tolerances. These changes narrow the process window, reduce throughput
and yields, and increase scrap, inspection, and qualification costs. At the same time, the

pool of suppliers able to produce M8 reliably at scale is much smaller, while AI-server
demand is accelerating, creating significantly tighter effective supply. That is why the M8
CCL ASP is more than double that of M7 grade CCL (Exhibit 9).
Once a material has been designed into a high-volume platform, changing it can require
renewed signal-integrity work, reliability testing and PCB-process validation. That creates
design-in persistence, and we believe a supplier’s qualification at M9 (for example) should

be viewed as more than a one-generation design win; it creates a cumulative advantage for
the next material transition. By the time a CCL supplier is qualified for M9, it has already
demonstrated that it can meet demanding electrical, thermal, dimensional-stability, and
manufacturability requirements at commercial scale. It has also accumulated valuable
process data, refined production yields, and developed working relationships with the end
customer, PCB fabricators, and upstream material suppliers. When the end customer

begins evaluating M10 or higher-grade materials, the incumbent can build from a proven
technical and manufacturing base rather than starting the qualification process from
scratch.
This advantage is reinforced by earlier access to customer roadmaps and opportunities for
joint development. A qualified M9 supplier is more likely to understand the customer’s
next-generation loss budget, stack-up constraints, reliability requirements, and production
timeline, allowing it to tailor its M10 product before broader qualification begins.

Customers also have an incentive to work with proven suppliers because changing
materials can require renewed signal-integrity modeling, PCB-process adjustments,

### Page 7

M
Foundation
Morgan Stanley Research 7
reliability testing, and yield validation. M9 qualification therefore does not guarantee
success at M10, as each generation can reopen competition, but it meaningfully improves
the probability of qualification, shortens time to market, and creates a compounding
technological and commercial lead.

Where are we in the cycle?
In our cycle framework, we place high-end CCL and HVLP copper foil at past the trough,
but still ahead of full earnings realization and peak-cycle conditions. Demand is being

driven by a multi-year migration toward higher layer-count PCBs and lower-loss materials,
while qualified supply remains constrained by long customer qualification cycles, lower
yields and upstream bottlenecks. We therefore expect mix, pricing and margins to improve
through 2027-28; however, the opportunity remains selective, as commodity-grade CCL
can stay oversupplied even as qualified high-end materials tighten, making this a stock-
selection cycle rather than a broad sector call.

Conclusion
We view the current demand cycle as being driven by a sustained rise in material
specifications rather than by a single product refresh. This distinction is important, as it
suggests the opportunity could be more structural and durable than previous electronics
cycles, which were often more dependent on unit shipments and shorter replacement
cycles.
In our view, the specification upgrades are also multiplicative rather than merely additive.

Moving to a higher-performance grade CCL typically requires simultaneous changes across
the material stack, involving more advanced resin systems, lower-profile copper foil, and
higher-grade glass cloth. At the same time, increasingly complex AI server and networking
architectures require PCBs with more layers, greater routing density, tighter signal-
integrity tolerances, and, in some cases, larger board dimensions. As a result, the value of
CCL, copper foil, and related materials used per system, or per rack, can continue to

increase even if the pace of server or rack shipment growth begins to moderate.
The main drivers of this content growth include:
• Migration toward higher-grade CCL. Rising data-transfer speeds, higher operating
frequencies, and greater thermal loads are increasing the need for low-loss, high-
speed CCL materials. As AI accelerators and networking systems move to faster
interconnect standards, electrical performance becomes increasingly sensitive to

dielectric loss, signal attenuation, and material consistency. This should support a
continued mix shift toward higher-grade CCLs with more advanced resin
formulations and tighter manufacturing requirements.
• Increasing PCB layer counts. AI servers, accelerator boards, and high-speed
switches require substantially more routing capacity to support a growing number
of processors, memory modules, power-delivery components, and high-speed
input/output channels. Higher layer counts allow designers to accommodate this

complexity while maintaining signal and power integrity. This increases the amount
of CCL and copper foil required per board and can also raise manufacturing
complexity and average selling prices.
Taken together, the continued migration toward higher-layer-count PCBs, lower-loss and
higher-speed CCL, more advanced copper foil, and potentially larger board formats should
support sustained growth in material content per system. We believe this specification-

driven upgrade cycle creates further revenue and earnings upside for the broader CCL and
copper-foil supply chain, particularly for suppliers that are already qualified on leading AI
server, accelerator, and networking platforms. This underappreciated content opportunity
is central to our positive industry view.

Stock implications
Elite Materials Co. (2383.TW, OW, PT NT$8,400)
EMC is a global leader in high-speed, low-loss CCL, with dominant market share across all

major GPU and ASIC customer platforms. It continues to invest for future growth, with
capacity expected to grow from 5,850k sheets/month at the end of 2025 to 11,250k
sheets/month by the end of 2028, or 92% growth. Most of these capacity additions will
be to support advanced grade CCL demand (M8+) over the next few years, driven by rising
demand for AI-related systems. We therefore forecast EMC's revenue to grow at a 76%
CAGR in 2025-2028, but we expect net profit to grow at a faster rate of 117% over the

same period. On EPS, our forecasts for 2026-28 are NT$122.17, NT$266.24, and NT
$416.24, respectively.
Price target and valuation discussion: Our price target of NT$8,400 implies 20x CY28 P/
E or 0.36x PEG, which we think is fair vs. its three year average of 14x because of the
strong revenue and profit outlook driven by higher grade CCLs. In the higher grade CCL
segment, there are also less capable suppliers, so competition decreases.
The 20x CY28 P/E implied by our price target is slightly above the past 3Y average +1SD

of 19x, but much lower than the 32x recent P/E peak. We deem this valuation as fair,
because EMC is benefitting from an earnings growth cycle fueled by stronger AI server
CCL demand, EMC's own mix improvement and continued pricing adjustments, which
supports margin expansion from 29.8% in 2025 to 41.4% by 2028 and an EPS CAGR of
117% over 2025-2028, on our estimates. Our 20x CY28 P/E for EMC is also higher than our

### Page 11
